find: The power of a lens is defined as \(P = \frac{1}{f}\), where \(f\) is the focal length in metres and power \(P\) is measured in dioptres (D). A short focal length means a high-power (strongly converging) lens. For a diverging lens, the focal length is negative, so the power is negative. Opticians prescribe spectacle lenses in dioptres: a \(+2\) D lens has a focal length of 0.5 m; a \(-4\) D lens has a focal length of −0.25 m.
replace: Colour comes from the way a material absorbs, transmits and reflects different wavelengths. A red jumper looks red because it reflects red light and absorbs the other colours. A red filter transmits red light and absorbs the rest — it does not add colour to the light. A white surface reflects all visible wavelengths; a black surface absorbs almost all of them. A smooth surface such as a mirror gives specular reflection, where the rays all leave in the same direction. A rough surface scatters the rays in many directions, which is why it looks matt instead of shiny.
